title: perf(canary): automated latency/throughput regression detection + rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve our continuous performance canary to automatically detect latency and throughput regressions and enforce rollout guards that prevent bad model/service rollouts. This PR implements a detector pipeline that compares recent canary windows against rolling baselines, introduces hysteresis to avoid flapping, and wires automatic abort/circuit-breaker policies into the rollout controller.

Summary of changes: added a new canary detector module (perf_canary.detector) that computes per-route latency P95/P99 and throughput deltas, threshold configuration with adaptive sensitivity, and KV-cache-aware thresholds to avoid false positives during warmup. Added rollout guard hooks to the rollout controller so canary failures cause automatic pause/abort with a reason and rollback artifact. Expanded telemetry (metrics/traces) and a new dashboard for canary trends + alerts. Added unit tests, integration tests that simulate regression scenarios, and a performance smoke test that runs against the perf-canary-lab runner. Updated docs: perf-canary README and operational runbook with guidance on tuning hysteresis and thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm + config schema
- [x] Rollout controller integration + abort reason propagation
- [x] Telemetry and dashboard (Grafana panel + alerts)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs + runbook
- [x] Manual canary e2e validation in staging

Behavioral notes: The detector evaluates windows of N requests (configurable per-customer) and computes relative regressions; it requires both statistical significance (sample size) and an absolute delta to fire. Hysteresis is applied via a two-window confirmation (fail then confirm) and minimum time between aborts to avoid noisy rollouts. The rollout controller supports three responses: pass, warn (annotate canary and continue), abort (pause rollout and optionally rollback).

CI history: initial run reported a flaky integration test (canary_simulation_test) that depended on wall-clock timing; replaced timing mocks and re-ran. Performance smoke was run in the perf-canary-lab and showed a 0.8% median latency regression on a synthetic high-concurrency workload vs baseline. That regression was due to a logging hot path and was fixed in commit 5. After fixes, perf-smoke signals within guard thresholds. Full CI: unit tests/pass, integration tests/pass after fix, perf-smoke/pass in staging.

Merge notes: squash-and-merged after approvals. See 'review_comments' for thread highlights and 'commits' for change breakdown.

References: Linear ENG-3245 (canary detection), ENG-3290 (rollout controller integration), runbook doc link: docs/perf-canary/runbook.md
